NQ · Asia 7–11 PM CT · London 1–4 AM CT · 1-min, 2024 – Oct 16 2026

Conditional Scenario Odds Explorer

Pick a session, a checkpoint and up to three things that are true right now. You see what happened next on past days that matched: how often, how far, and when. Both sides always show. The tick on each bar is the all-days base rate.

Verdicts

In plain English

    Scenario table

    Depth = how far past the level it went on the days it happened (median, middle half). × = that depth as a multiple of the range it is measured against (session range so far, prior session range, or overnight range). Time = median clock time (CT) of the extreme or the first break. Flag: FDR = differs from the all-days rate on 2024–25 after the whole-universe correction; then 2026 (unseen) held / same sign / flipped. Cells under 30 days are marked thin; under 15 are hidden.

    Decision tree

    Each level splits the days by one state. Bars show the outcome mix on that branch; the root row is all days. Branches with fewer than 15 days are faded. * = the branch's leading outcome beats the all-days rate after the correction on 2024–25 and held in 2026.

    Top reads that held in 2026

    One- and two-state cells, n ≥ 30, sorted by strength on 2024–25. "Location" reads follow from where price sits (closer to a level → it breaks first); "context" reads use only yesterday, the calendar or Asia's size. Click a row to open it in the table.

    Live: ask any question

    The tables above are fixed checkpoints. cso_live.py answers any event-shaped question at any minute by running a fresh backtest over every 1-min day since 2020 (about 5 seconds). When the exact match has fewer than 30 days, it drops one condition at a time (the one that frees the most days) and shows every step, ending with the events-only base. Every % has an 80% range.

    CommandWhat it does
    python -I cso_live.py --nowReads your TradingView chart, finds what just happened (biggest impulse in the last 30 min, levels just taken, where price sits) and answers 3–5 questions with today's prices.
    python -I cso_live.py --ask "…" --liveYour own question; --live adds today's price for every level and lets you write now / now-30.
    python -I cso_live.py --serveThe watcher: keeps 15 years of 1-min bars in memory, reads the chart every minute (6 PM–4 PM CT) into cso/live_latest.txt / .json, and answers the commands below in about 2–3 s (a brand-new question about 10 s).
    --fastOnly the answer step plus the shape step, one compact table each. Every row says how soon: median minutes and the clock time that lands today.
    NY morningLevels: 8:30 open, first 15-min bar, IB (from 9:30), NY VWAP, overnight high/low, yesterday's noon–3 PM, prior day. Reads: open-drive, first bar and Crabel stretch, the same rules as the bots. On FOMC/CPI/NFP days it matches same-kind days first and says when it had to fall back.
    python -I cso_live.py --q "odds of hitting .786"Plain English on top of the live read: "new london high", "back to the asia low", "which first .618 or new high", "london high or london low first".
    --draw / --clearPuts the impulse's fib levels on your TradingView chart with their odds ("0.786 · 64% in 60 min · n 41"). Never saved to the layout; --clear removes them.
    python -I cso_live.py --calibrationEvery live answer is logged. This checks what actually happened and shows called vs happened by 10% bucket, plus a Brier score.
    --oldAdds a 2011–19 column (side note only; conclusions stay 2024–26).
    --alerts · --journal 2026-10-28 [--trades fills.csv]Which known setups just completed (dry run: Discord posting waits for a webhook) · a session journal page with the chart, levels, every question asked and what happened.
    python -I cso_live.py --testRe-checks tonight's hand-built answers (22, 48, 32 and 17 days, all match), the already-passed guard, the timing ladder and the calibration math.
    Already-passed guard. If a level was reached before the moment you ask about, that day doesn't count as a hit for that level. It is set aside, and the table says what share was set aside. Before this, tonight's "62% retrace before a new high: 82%" counted days that had already hit 62% during the 12-minute wait. On days where 62% was still untouched, it was 2 of 5 (40%), too few to lean on.
    When the exact state is rare, it still answers: timing conditions loosen first (±50%), then conditions drop one at a time, and a shape rung adds the 40 past days whose last 75 minutes looked most like now, with their dates so you can replay them.

    How to ask

    PartWordsMeans
    Levelsasia_hi asia_lo · london_hi london_lo · on_hi on_lo · pdh pdl pdc · X.level X.top X.size · asia_lo-20Asia 7–11 PM; London 1 AM to now; overnight since 5 PM; prior NY 8:30–3; levels from an event named X; any level ± points.
    Stateat 2:45 · swept asia_hi · unswept asia_lo · inside asia · pos asia 0.6 1 · above pdh · dow 1 2 3 4 · event fomcFilters known at that moment. Times are CT, 24-hour (2:45 = 2:45 AM, 15:00 = 3 PM).
    Eventsbreak LEVEL [to T] as B · newlow london [from T] [any] as L · impulse up 60 within 7 as I · reclaim B within 5 maxdepth 20 · nohigh I.top 12 · cond retrace I >= 0.382 within 12Things that happen in order. Each moves the clock forward; outcomes start at the next bar, so nothing after it leaks in.
    Outcomes?hit london_hi by 3:59 8:29 15:00 · ?retrace I 0.382 0.5 0.618 1 within 30 60 · ?race above I.top vs retrace I 0.618 · ?extremes by 8:29 · ?lodhod% of days, depth past the level, median minutes; races report which came first.
